nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants remove the CIROP protease. The source describes the five genes its screen found as encoding extracellular proteins, so CIROP acts in the space around the left-right organizer rather than inside its cells.

evidence.snippet: We further ascertained 21 human patients with loss-of-function CIROP mutations presenting with recessive situs anomalies.

evidence.reference_title: Discovery of a genetic module essential for assigning left-right asymmetry in humans and ancestral vertebrates.
evidence.snippet: We searched for genes whose loss during vertebrate evolution follows this pattern and identified five genes encoding extracellular proteins, including a putative protease with hitherto unknown functions that we named ciliated left-right organizer metallopeptide (CIROP).

evidence.reference_title: Genetic Analysis of Heterotaxy in a Consanguineous Cohort.
evidence.snippet: Genetic analysis, with exome sequencing, genome sequencing, or multigene panel, detected 9 unique variants, 7 of which were novel, in 8 genes known to be implicated in autosomal recessive form of HTX (C1orf127, CCDC39, CIROP, DNAAF3, DNAH5, DNAH9, MMP21, and MNS1) providing a yield of 42.1%.

nodes.description: Congenital heart disease is close to obligate in this cohort: nearly all 21 patients had one. The manuscript does not tabulate the individual lesions in the text available here, so the binding is the general cardiac morphology term rather than a specific malformation.

evidence.reference_title: A functional operon delineates an extracellular pathway that controls body asymmetry only in animals with a ciliated left-right organizer
evidence.snippet: Of the 21 cases ... presenting with congenital heterotaxy, 8 had situs solitus with or without isolated ... dextrocardia, 5 had situs ambiguus, 8 had situs inversus totalis, and nearly all had congenital ... heart defects (CHD).

nodes.description: Isolated dextrocardia occurred in some of the 8 patients whose visceral situs was otherwise normal. The source groups them as situs solitus with or without isolated dextrocardia, so it does not give a separate count.

nodes.description: Without a reliable asymmetric signal the embryo cannot distinguish left from right, and organ situs is assigned inconsistently across the body, which is what heterotaxy is.

evidence.reference_title: Discovery of a genetic module essential for assigning left-right asymmetry in humans and ancestral vertebrates.
evidence.snippet: Our findings posit the existence of an ancestral genetic module that has twice disappeared during vertebrate evolution but remains essential for distinguishing left from right in humans.

nodes.description: The defect sits between the cilia and the first asymmetric gene. In zebrafish and Xenopus CIROP is required only on the left, downstream of the leftward flow and upstream of DAND5. So the cilia and the flow they generate are intact, and what fails is the conversion of that flow into a side-specific signal. This separates CIROP-related heterotaxy from the ciliopathic laterality disorders, where the cilia themselves are at fault.

evidence.reference_title: Discovery of a genetic module essential for assigning left-right asymmetry in humans and ancestral vertebrates.
evidence.snippet: In zebrafish and Xenopus, CIROP is required solely on the left side, downstream of the leftward flow, but upstream of DAND5, the first asymmetrically expressed gene.

nodes.description: DAND5 is the first asymmetrically expressed gene, and its Xenopus ortholog Coco is a Nodal inhibitor whose left-sided downregulation is the direct readout of the leftward flow. A defect upstream of DAND5 therefore leaves the Nodal cascade without the side-specific release of repression that normally orients it. The Nodal-antagonist step is carried by work on the ortholog rather than by the CIROP report itself, which is why its evidence item is INDIRECT.

evidence.reference_title: The nodal inhibitor Coco is a critical target of leftward flow in Xenopus.
evidence.snippet: Coco thus acts as a critical target of flow, suggesting that symmetry is broken by flow-mediated left-asymmetric release of Nodal repression at the midline.

nodes.description: Situs anomalies, the reported presentation in all 21 patients. The author manuscript breaks the cohort down: 8 had situs solitus with or without isolated dextrocardia, 5 had situs ambiguus and 8 had situs inversus totalis. HPO has no separate situs ambiguus term, so that group is covered by this Heterotaxy row and the two positional findings are recorded separately below.

nodes.description: CIROP is expressed specifically in left-right organizers that carry motile cilia, so the loss is confined to the transient embryonic structure that sets the body axis. This node records where the protease acts, not a process outcome, so it carries no biological-process binding; the left-right determination terms sit on the nodes that record the failing process.
